newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: ROWING-REDGRAVE AND CO MAINTAIN UNBEATEN RUN.
newsitem.headline: ROWING-REDGRAVE AND CO MAINTAIN UNBEATEN RUN.

text.p: Britain's coxless four, led by four times Olympic champion Steve Redgrave, maintained their unbeaten record with victory at the Rowing World Cup on Sunday.

The British crew, which was formed in April, won their eighth successive race and third straight World Cup event, but their efforts caused barely a ripple as Germany surged to overall victory in the inaugural series on the Rotsee lake.

Redgrave and double Olympic champion Matthew Pinsent, who had previously been a formidable combination in the coxless pairs, have their sights set on Olympic glory at the 2000 Games in Sydney in a boat with Tim Foster and James Cracknell.
"We started from scratch this year -- it doesn't matter if we lose all of our races as long as we win the Olympic Games," said Redgrave.
The British quartet took the lead at the 500-metre mark and surged away at the 1,750-metre post to finish in five minutes 53.09 seconds, more than two seconds clear of the second-placed Romanians.

The German national team went into the final regatta of the three-event series with a commanding overall lead and extended that advantage with five victories in the 14 races to take both the Lucerne regatta trophy and the overall World Cup.
They won the men's quadruple sculls and lightweight double sculls, the women's double and quadruple sculls and the men's eight to finish on 209 points, well ahead of Britain on 101 and Romania on 88.
